claim: Vision-language systems can produce definite answers that supplied evidence does not justify. We study entailed, contradicted and underdetermined strict-left-of relations with symbolic ground truth and explicitly separated behavioral, representation and intervention evidence. A legacy audit finds conditional label predictability despite logically insufficient individual premises. We construct 9,216 fully counterbalanced development variants across six families: audited nonsemantic feature ceilings are 1/3 balanced accuracy, single-modality oracle-parsed role ceilings are 2/3, and the joint symbolic oracle reaches 1. These are design diagnostics, not model performance. A process-isolated 12-forward pilot compares two frozen compact VLMs on one fixed No/Undetermined pair. SmolVLM2 selects Yes/Yes; Qwen3-VL selects No/Yes, exactly reproducing earlier Qwen scores. Both give an unsupported definite answer on the fork; candidate-length normalization changes Qwen rankings. Historical CE50 and CE+ES5 development results remain unmatched-budget exploratory evidence, while selected probes and failed negative controls establish no relation-specific mechanism. We provide preserved raw outputs, controlled benchmark sources and CPU audits. The matched pilot is too small for three-class accuracy or generalization claims. Independent evaluation, end-to-end unimodal baselines, causal evidence, objective benefit and material novelty remain unresolved.

claim: Let R(x,y) mean that x is strictly left of y. On distinct objects with consistent spatial evidence, R is irreflexive, asymmetric, and transitive. Let E be the supplied premises and q=R(A,C). The label is Yes when E entails q; No when E entails not-q; and Undetermined when E entails neither q nor not-q. Inconsistent premise sets require a separate rejection policy and are outside this three-state formalization.
